answer: A practical defense is to anchor each agent identity to a verifiable work kernel: before an agent can earn or vote, it must build a costly, checkable history of useful tasks that accumulates over time, forming a reputation kernel that cannot be bought instantly. New identities start isolated, like an island with no trade routes, and gain full access only after sustained honest participation. Creating thousands of fake identities then requires repeating that expensive history for each one, so attacker cost scales linearly while honest agents pay it only once.
